anti_patterns.correct: Shuffle/randomize input before loading — sorted data causes lock contention and deadlocks, degrading throughput by 2-10x
Always drain the redo queue after loading — redo records complete deferred entity resolution; skipping leaves results incomplete
Disable synchronous_commit during bulk loads (PostgreSQL: ALTER SYSTEM SET synchronous_commit = 'off'), re-enable after — 5-20x throughput improvement

anti_patterns.pattern: Initialize Factory/Environment per call or thread
anti_patterns.correct: Initialize once per process, share across threads — factory/environment is thread-safe; per-call init causes memory leaks and conflicts

compatibility_notes:
LICENSE REQUIRED: You have 755000 records, which exceeds the default Senzing license limit of 500. The user must choose one of:
1) Request an evaluation license — email sales@senzing.com with name, company, email, number of records (755000), and date
2) Provide a license they already have — place the license file at the path specified by SENZING_LICENSE_FILE or in the etc/ directory
3) Load only the first 500 records as a sample
HARDWARE SIZING: Call search_docs(query='hardware sizing capacity planning') for minimum specs and capacity planning guidance.

WARNING: If your input data was not produced by mapping_workflow, run it through mapping_workflow first. Hand-mapped data commonly has: wrong attribute names (e.g., EMPLOYER_NAME instead of NAME_ORG, PHONE instead of PHONE_NUMBER — see field-aliases via mapping_workflow for the correct catalog names), missing RECORD_TYPE (degrades organization resolution), and missing ADDR_TYPE for organizations. These issues silently degrade entity resolution quality without producing load errors. Note: the flat/legacy shape (feature attributes at the record root, or per-feature named sub-lists) is NOT one of these problems — the Entity Specification still supports it; only the attribute NAMES and RECORD_TYPE/ADDR_TYPE coverage matter for resolution quality.
